newsitem.title: UK: UK's Blair offers BP head key European role - report.
newsitem.headline: UK's Blair offers BP head key European role - report.

text.p: Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair is offering British Petroleum chairman Sir David Simon a leading government role in shaping policy towards the European Union, the Financial Times reported on Saturday.
"The new prime minister is understood to have offered Sir David the position of minister for Europe and a seat in the Lords (the upper house of parliament)," the newspaper said.
It gave no source for its information but quoted an unidentified friend of Simon as saying: "He would like to have a role with the government but is also committed to staying at BP."
The Financial Times said the discussions indicated that Blair was intent on taking a constructive approach towards EU negotiations.
"Sir David is a strong supporter of the EU and European monetary union," said the newspaper.

No independent confirmation of the report was immediately available on Saturday as Britain embarked on a new era of politics with its youngest prime minister this century facing up to the realities of power after his Labour Party's 18 years of opposition.
